acceptance: Only complete, intentional references are recognised (a URL, a Markdown or wiki link, an explicit workspace path; a bare file name or a sentence with a URL is text); unsafe protocols, credentials and control characters are denied before the host sees them; a resolved, an ambiguous (offering its candidates) or a not-yet-loaded workspace reference with candidates and an external link can open while a missing or denied one cannot.

reason: TS hosts declare their navigation capabilities, so a host without external opening reports external links unavailable, and a host may cancel a workspace open or return no outcome that the port must preserve. Every native editor host opens external links through the app and requests workspace opens as fire-and-forget events, so there is no missing capability or returned outcome.

acceptance: One guide per complete indentation level at the configured unit and tab width, none for partial whitespace, stopping at the first non-whitespace character (capped at sixteen).

reason: These guard TS's adapter onto CodeMirror's private measurement queue (a queued measure must run synchronously through public APIs, and an engine upgrade that stops flushing must fail loudly). The native code editor lays text out itself and has no third-party measurement queue.

acceptance: An image pasted into an HTML page is written beside the document as a new `image-<uuid>` file whose bytes match its PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP name; SVG, mislabelled, empty and over-20 MiB files and names with a path are refused without writing, nothing is replaced, and a failed write is reported.

reason: TS relays a framed page's scroll and pointer into the host document as DOM custom events in the host's coordinates. Native web views report their own scroll and pointer to the GPUI view that owns them, with no DOM between.

acceptance: SQLite names in any case route to the lazy database preview that reads a resource session in a native worker, never a full-file buffer; a `.db` file keeps the generic binary MIME and generic binary data never routes to the database preview.

Saving an App's setup first checks that what it launches exists: a missing package script is refused before anything is written, an advanced package-manager command is not mistaken for a script, and a setup whose script exists is saved against the content the page read.
